external.name: pi-lens
external.review: MIT; Node >=22.19.0. Static review of the supplied 4.4.4 package only; no package code executed or TUI/model-provider validation. Native @ast-grep/napi ^0.50.0, @ast-grep/cli 0.50.0 (dependency lifecycle platform binary setup), bundled core/vendor tree-sitter WASM and optional web-tree-sitter 0.25.10; no runtime typescript dependency. No preinstall/install/postinstall in this manifest; prepare is a source-build hook (build, grammar download, git hooks, lock stamping, loader warming), not a registry-install hook. Registers 13 pi tools: adds symbol_search, project_report, effective_config, lens_diagnostic_mark and pi_lens_activate_tools; removes ast_grep_dump, ast_dump and standalone lsp_diagnostics. Exact firewall entries allow analysis/config/discovery, ask for structural replacement, LSP navigation and diagnostic suppression; path checks include paths arrays and analysisRoot (tests/tool-firewall-smoke.ts, tests/firewall-shell-smoke.ts). Diagnostics also run in process through session/write/edit/turn hooks, outside tool-call isolation. Profiles select the companion as a whole; balanced does not filter its registered tools. The earlier dependency warning applies to 3.8.63: 4.4.4 declares optional peers pi-coding-agent=* and pi-tui=*, typebox=^1.0.0. pi 1.3 warns on host packages in dependencies, not this manifest, though typebox still differs from the recommended wildcard. The kit defaults PI_LENS_DISABLE_LSP_INSTALL=1 and PI_LENS_DISABLE_TOOL_INSTALL=1; 4.4.4 honours both, including managed refreshes. Existing tools keep working. Missing non-vendored grammar downloads are separately trust-gated and not disabled by these switches; hash checking depends on a matching grammars.lock.json entry. See docs/supply-chain.md for the registration diff and limits.

external.name: pi-lean-ctx
external.review: Apache-2.0. OPT-IN, in no profile: it needs the external `lean-ctx` Rust CLI (`cargo install lean-ctx` or brew; not bundled, not in this package's supply chain) and, in its default additive mode, registers extra model-visible tools even when that CLI is absent (ctx_shell, ctx_read, ctx_ls, ctx_find, ctx_grep, lean_ctx, ctx_edit; checked against 3.11.4 in a real pi 1.3.0 TUI with a scratch agent directory). When the CLI is present, its MCP bridge also registers whatever tools the lean-ctx MCP server lists (extensions/mcp-bridge.ts registerMcpTool). Those tools are not inspected the way the built-in ones are: secret-guard matches the built-in names bash/write/edit, so ctx_shell and ctx_edit are outside its checks, and tool-firewall sees them only as unknown tools (policy default: ask) rather than as shell commands. Enable it only for trusted repositories and expect an approval prompt per call; it is installed by `install.ts --all` only when its binary is on PATH. 3.11.4 static review against 3.10.5: no dependencies, no install lifecycle scripts (prepack/pretest only build the vendor bundle), the same seven registered tools and the same peers (typebox ^1.0.0, pi-tui *, pi-coding-agent >=0.74.0); source changes are SPDX headers, one parameter description and the version constant. Its self-contained extensions/vendor/mcp-sdk.cjs (MCP Client and StdioClientTransport) is rebuilt from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.32.1 instead of ^1.29.0. GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw (1.24.0 to 1.31.0) affects only servers that pass a taskStore, so the bundled client was never exposed to it, but a scanner matching the SDK version would flag the old bundle; OSV and npm audit cannot see a vendored bundle, so moving the pin is the only way to update it. Verified to load and degrade gracefully without the CLI. Replaces 3.10.5.

external.name: pi-readseek
external.review: MIT. @jarkkojs/readseek (native) + xxhash-wasm. Hash-anchored read/edit/grep + structural code maps + AST search — a lean file-I/O primitive for navigating large repos cheaply. Registers replacement tools (manual). OSV reports no advisories for a fresh 0.4.26 install. 0.12.0 (latest, published 2026-10-23) was evaluated against its tarball and in pi 1.3.0 with a scratch agent directory, and not adopted: it is a different tool surface, not an update. It no longer replaces read/edit/write/grep by default; it adds 16 tools (readSeek_show, _tree, _meta, _assets, _syntax, _check, _caption, _objects, _ocr, _search, _grep, _def, _refs, _edit, _rename, _write) beside the built-ins, which more than doubles the active tool-definition size measured in pi (7,033 to 15,845 characters) and works against the lite profile. Its `readseek.overrideTools` setting is read only from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and .pi/settings.json, ignoring PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR. readSeek_check `rules` and readSeek_search `rule` accept `@path` file references that the firewall's path fields do not see, so allow entries would let them read credential files unchecked. readSeek_caption/_objects/_ocr run locally installed vision models. The licence is Apache-2.0 and the linux-x64 AppImage is LGPL-3.0-or-later; it depends on @jarkkojs/readseek-api (bundling @sinclair/typebox 0.34.52 and @bgotink/kdl). Adopting it needs exact firewall entries for all 16 tools, `@path` handling in the classifier and a decision on the lite surface; 0.4.26 stays pinned until then.
